name: Proto 230: Auto MAC addresses
description: Every MAC on the mesh is worked out from something that never changes, so there is no table to keep.

nodes.name: The MAC scheme (52:54:...)
nodes.description: 0x52 has the locally-administered bit set, so these never clash with real hardware.

nodes.name: VM MAC 52:54:00:II:II:II
nodes.description: The first three bytes of the VM's id: same id, same MAC, wherever it runs.

nodes.name: Storage MAC 52:54:24:II:II:II
nodes.description: The same three id bytes under 52:54:24, for the VM's NIC on 10.24.

nodes.name: Bridge MAC 52:54:00:23:BB:fe
nodes.description: Box BB's overlay bridge: bootstrap sets it from the box number.

nodes.name: Slot MACs 52:54:00:23:BB:00-0f
nodes.description: 16 per box, in the derived FDB today; VMs on them (and SLAAC from them) are planned for 3.0.

nodes.name: VM id (UUID)
nodes.description: Never changes: not on migration, not on rename (VMs were renamed 2026-11-27; their MACs stayed).

nodes.name: Box number
nodes.description: Given out by the cluster CA when a box joins.

nodes.name: libvirt domain XML
nodes.description: xdebbied writes `<mac address=...>` into each VM's definition.

nodes.name: VM network config
nodes.description: cloud-init matches the primary NIC by MAC and runs DHCP on it.

nodes.name: xdebbied DHCP responder
nodes.description: Answers on the bridge: finds the VM whose MAC is the request's chaddr and gives it its 10.23 address.

nodes.name: Bridge FDB
nodes.description: Where each MAC lives: static entries for bridges in derived mode, learned ones for VMs.

relationships.description: The MAC scheme (52:54:...) has VM MAC 52:54:00:II:II:II.
The MAC scheme (52:54:...) has Storage MAC 52:54:24:II:II:II.
The MAC scheme (52:54:...) has Bridge MAC 52:54:00:23:BB:fe.
The MAC scheme (52:54:...) has Slot MACs 52:54:00:23:BB:00-0f.
xdebbied takes the id's first three bytes.
Same bytes, different prefix, so the two NICs never collide.
The box number goes in the fifth byte.
The MAC goes into the domain XML.
And into the VM's network config.
The VM asks for an address from that MAC.
The responder knows the answer without a lease table: the MAC says which VM it is.
Peers point a static entry at each box's bridge MAC (derived mode).
VM MACs are learned as they talk (learn mode, which the boxes run today).

flows.name: A VM gets its addresses
flows.description: From an id to a working address, with nothing stored on the way.

transitions.description: The VM's id gives its MAC.
The VM's network config matches on it.
The VM asks for an address.
xdebbied answers from the MAC alone.
The other boxes learn where it lives as it talks.
